description: Beginner with no paying clients: training exercise, one deliverable and limited feedback, without validated demand.

echanges.question: Tell me about the last time someone chose you.
echanges.reponse: I have never had a client. During my course, two classmates asked me to reorganise the home page for our fictional library project. It was not commercial work.

echanges.question: What did you do personally?
echanges.reponse: I grouped the information and designed a mock-up. One classmate wrote the text; the other wrote the code. I did not test the page with real users.

echanges.question: What feedback did you receive?
echanges.reponse: Both classmates found the mock-up clearer. Our instructor said the headings helped people scan the page. I cannot infer that the page would be used more.

echanges.question: What remains unknown?
echanges.reponse: I do not know which organisations would need this or whether anyone would pay. I have no other project to describe and no usage measurement.

echanges.question: What boundary do you want to set?
echanges.reponse: I want to show this exercise as an exercise. I do not want to say I helped a real library or promise new readers.

echanges.question: What can you check now?
echanges.reponse: I can prepare a short introduction and show it privately to someone who runs an association. I want to understand which situations they recognise, without mistaking a compliment for an order.

faits_a_conserver: Fictional training project, no paying clients and no real users observed.
Individual contribution: organising information and designing a mock-up; classmates wrote the text and code.
Feedback from two classmates and the instructor, without usage measurement.
Commercial audiences and willingness to pay are unknown.
affirmations_interdites: Validated market, acquired customers or demonstrated willingness to pay.
Personal inferiority or inability inferred from having no clients.
criteres: The four axes assess only support in the account, without an average, personal worth score or inferred market demand.
Confidence expresses interpretive uncertainty, not a scientific probability.
Evidence quotes exactly one answer and its existing turn; no described record is presented as verified by Atlas.
heritage is null and evitements stays empty: none of these scenarios reports a deliberate omission.
The bio is a proposed professional statement bounded by the facts, never a definitive identity.
There is one reversible, observable next step feasible within 48 hours; suggested pistes are optional, at most three.
For an interview follow-up: one open question of at most ten words; corrections are applied and boundaries respected.
Missing accounts of boundaries being tested do not establish that they have never been tested.
The mock-up and text have different authors; the account does not attribute the heading choices.
A proposed outside exchange does not establish that nobody outside the course has seen the work.
